title: Hemolysis Test of Human Erythrocytes
author: Germán Alberto Téllez Ramírez
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.jh9cj96

steps.title: Prepare Erythrocyte Suspension
steps.instruction: Isolate and wash human erythrocytes from heparinized blood.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge 2 ml of heparinized blood at 800 g for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Wash the erythrocyte pellet three times with normotonic washing solution by centrifuging at 800 g for 10 minutes each time.
Resuspend the erythrocytes in a volume of normotonic washing solution equal to the initial blood volume.

steps.title: Prepare Erythrocyte Working Solution
steps.instruction: Dilute the erythrocyte stock and incubate.

substeps.instruction: Dilute the erythrocyte stock solution 1:250 with 1X PBS.
Incubate the working solution for 15 minutes at 37°C.

steps.title: Prepare Sample Dilutions
steps.instruction: Prepare a 10X stock of the sample and perform serial dilutions.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a 10X concentration of the sample relative to the final evaluation concentration (starting from a stock of 1 mg/mL to 5 mg/mL).
Perform 1:1 serial dilutions starting from the most concentrated sample to the most dilute required using 1X PBS as diluent.

steps.title: Set Up Microplate
steps.instruction: Dispense sample concentrations and controls into a 96-well microplate.

substeps.instruction: Add 10 µL of each 10X sample concentration in triplicate to the wells.
For positive controls: add 10 µL of 0.1% v/v Triton X-100 to achieve a final concentration of 0.01%.
For negative controls: add 10 µL of diluent (1X PBS).

steps.title: Incubate Samples with Erythrocytes
steps.instruction: Add erythrocyte working solution and incubate the plate.

substeps.instruction: Add 90 µL of the erythrocyte working solution to each well.
Add erythrocytes in order from lowest to highest concentration to reuse tips and avoid cross-contamination.
Incubate the plate for 2 hours at 37°C.

steps.title: Separate Supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the plate and collect the supernatant.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge the plate at 800 g for 5 minutes.
Carefully extract the supernatant (approximately 80 µL/well) and transfer it to another microplate.

steps.title: Measure Absorbance
steps.instruction: Read the absorbance of the collected supernatants using a spectrophotometer at 540 nm.

steps.title: Calculate Hemolysis Percentage
steps.instruction: Process the absorbance data to determine the percentage of hemolysis.

substeps.instruction: Calculate the median absorbance of the blank (diluent) and subtract this value (delta) from all well absorbance values.
Calculate the median of these delta values for each treatment or concentration.
Calculate the percentage of hemolysis for each well by multiplying the delta absorbance by 100% and dividing by the median absorbance of the positive control (100% hemolysis).
